text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- SERBIA
NASA BORBA

- Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos and Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic express concern over situation in Albania because of possible negative consequences on the neighbouring countries, discuss bilateral cooperation.
- Belgrade University Council elects director of hospital centre Bezanijska Kosa Momcilo Babic as president and Dragan Kuburovic as acting rector of Belgrade University.

- U.S. Congressman Nick Rayhal denies receiving letter of Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic about the republic's rediness to declare independence from Yugoslavia that was published in Belgrade newspaper Politka.
- The Yugoslav parliament to approve new Yugoslav government Thursday.

- Speaker of the Federal Parliament Chamber of Citizens calls opposition coalition Zajedno deputies to attend federal parliament session and endorse their mandates. Democratic party, one of the coalition members, said the coalition would not participate because there is no live TV coverage.
- Federal parliament foreign policy committee supports special ties agreement between Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serb republic which to be endorsed by parliament today.
- Serbian war invalids to stage protest on March 27 because the state is not paying out their pensions.
- Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce committee for economic system asks federal government to abolish customs duties and taxes on imports of industrial equipment which range from 13 to 50 percent.
- Serbian privatisation law to be presented on Monday, March 24.
- Italian firm Italgas and Oil Industry of Serbia NIS Energogas to make study on developpment of gas network for Belgrade and other Serbian towns.
- President of Yugoslav Left JUL Ljubisa Ristic says Socialist Pary of Serbia, JUL and Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro DPS have reached full agreement on new government members.
- BK TV will suffer 100 million German marks of damages if PTT Serbia really cuts off its broadcasts and will file a suit.

- Belgrade bank Beogradska Banka appoints Borka Vucic, hitherto director of its Cyprus branch, as acting general manager. Present general manager Ljubisa Igic is appointed general manager of the Anglo-Yugoslav Bank in London.
POLITIKA
- Oil industry Serbia NIS Jugopetrol and Sinochem from Peking sign another five-year business agreement. Present one-year agreement expires on March 31.
- Washington Times editor says he did not receive denial from Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic of the letter in which he wants to topple Yugoslavia.
- Italian parliamentary delegation says Kosovo issue should be resolved without changing Yugoslavia's outer borders.
- New round of bilateral succession talks on the former Yugoslavia to be in April, says head of Yugoslav delegation Kosta Mihajlovic.
- Farmers need long-term loans for spring sowing which banks unable to privide, it was said at the banking comitte of the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce.
- Yugoslav average wage in February was 695 dinars which is up 12.5 percent on January, say statistics.
- Yugoslav government will participate in financing of study for privatisation of steel industry by 2010, to be done by French consulting firm Usinor.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Experts of Vienna's atomic energy agency say situation with radioactive waste disposal at Vinca institute near Belgrade is alarming. Institute officials deny reports that barrels containing highly radioactive waste are corroding.

- Final make-up of new Yugoslav government not yet known before today's session of federal parliament. Parliament expected to verify agreement on special ties between Yugoslavia and the Bosnian Serb Republic.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Preferential treatment for Yugoslav exports to 15 countries of the European Union could be restored on March 24, Politika Ekspres learns.
- Co-owner of independent Belgrade newspaper Blic Peter Kelbel sentenced by court in Graz, Austria, to two years in prison for fraud.
-- MONTENEGRO
POBJEDA

- U.S. congressmen Bruce Vento and Nick Reichel refute authenticity of March 18 letter by Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic published in Politika on Wednesday. Government says another such letter allegedly sent to Washington Post also a fake.

- Opposition deputy in Montenegrin parliament Stefan Susic publicly backs Djukanovic, saying that if the Serbian regime assumes the right to topple Montenegro's prime minister, then there there is no equality between the federal units in Yugoslavia.

- Montenegro wants a strong and democratic state, but if our federal partner chooses differently, then Yugoslavia will never survive in its present form, Culture Minister Goran Rakocevic tells Japanese daily Sekai Nipo.
- Yugoslav Army ends exercises in area of Lake Skadar and River Bojana, on Albanian border.
- Bosnian Serb delegation visits Montenegrin Ministry of Transport.
- Government/university delegation signs protocol of cooperation with Bari university in Italy.
- 450 Norwegian rheumatism patients to be treated in Igalo health resort this summer - contract signed March 19 by Health Institute and Norwegian Health Ministry.
